# Methods: Kinnex array integrity (main text)

Three Kinnex 8-fold libraries were made from FLIGHT-seq cDNA of one BD Rhapsody cartridge, split after lysis: with no TSO-TSO depletion, with a home-made biotin-Read1 pulldown, or with the Kinnex TSO artifact removal. Each was sequenced on one Revio SMRT Cell. Every analysis used a hash sample of 18% of each cell's ZMWs (1.97 to 2.08 million HiFi reads per library). We searched each HiFi read on both strands with edlib for the nine Kinnex adapters (up to 2 edits), the TSO core and Read1 (up to 3 edits each), kept an adapter hit only within 4 bp of a TSO or Read1 hit, and cut the read at its adapters. Each molecule was classed by the primers at its two ends, and each read by its chain of adapters as complete, truncated, mirror or other. skera's S-reads were matched to these molecules by their coordinates in the parent read; a gap between two consecutive S-reads with no adapter of ours within 5 bp was counted as a false cut. lima 2.13.0, isoseq refine 4.3.0 and the mapped fltnc BAM of the standard Iso-Seq workflow gave the fate of each S-read. The public ArgenTag MDA-MB-453 8-fold dataset was annotated in the same way. The full methods are in the Supplementary Note; the code, and every number with its source table, are in the flight-kinnex-qc repository.
